title: His early drum set and wooden pedal
summary: Bass drum, snare, cymbal, wood blocks and car bells; no tom-toms or hi-hat, and a wooden overhead pedal.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Early drum kits and the gear drummers used

blocks.x: What was your drum set like? How many traps and all did you have? A snare and bass drum, anything else? Simple?
This bass drum at that time, I mean, bass drum and snare drum and cymbal at that time.
Have any tom-toms or wood blocks?
No, no. Wood blocks, yeah. Wood blocks, yeah. Wood blocks, yeah.
I had no tom-toms, didn't use no tom-toms in that time. Did you have no bells?
Yeah, car bells, car bells. No tom-toms, didn't use any tom-toms in that time.
Yeah. Did you have any of the hi-hat cymbal ever? Did you?
No, nothing there was no. Sock cymbal? No, there was no wear on. Never. Ain't nobody had nothing like that.
What kind of a foot pedal did you have on that? The same as they make it now?
No, I had overhead when I first saw that overhead. Oh, yeah. Hook it with a strap, I mean. In other words, it was a wood pedal.
Wood pedal. That didn't, that's one of those kind that hit the cymbal at the same time you hit the drum?
That's right, that's right. But you could stop it from hitting the cymbal. I had a piece that you could shove it back and it wouldn't hit the cymbal.
Leave it like a little hammer. If you hit the cymbal, then it wouldn't slowly push it down. Push it back.
